note: WP-42 adds layout, a stage question and a way to ask. Every statement of fact in the new copy was already published on /pricing/ before this package, or is a plain restatement of src/data/packages.ts. The entries below map each new block to its origin. No amount, seat count, date, statistic, person, company or testimonial is introduced.

sources.title: The four package names, stage-fit sentences and depths
sources.exact_url_or_locator: src/data/packages.ts, packages (captured by WP-40 as wp40-pricing-table)
sources.variables_units_scope: PackageCards (name, stage-fit sentence, depth), the PackagePicker radio and list text, the picker status sentence ('<Name> is sized for this stage: <stage fit> Its depth in every service line is <depth>.') and the Composer banner ('Sized for: <stage fit>'). The sentences are rendered from the data module, not retyped.

sources.title: Short stage labels
sources.next_review: Any change to the stage-fit sentences
sources.variables_units_scope: Four labels: 'Idea or prototype', 'First product', 'Early customer evidence', 'Several products, or a regulated field'. Each is a shortening of the stage-fit sentence of the same package (an idea or a prototype; a first product; early customer evidence; several products, or a regulated or capital-intensive field). Used where the full sentence does not fit: the card eyebrow, a Composer select option and the picker. The sentence always appears beside it.
sources.methodology_limitations: Derived wording, not quoted. A unit test checks that every word of a label appears in its sentence.
sources.freshness_trigger: Any change to the stage-fit sentences

sources.variables_units_scope: SeatExplainer: 'A seat is one dedicated place on your team.'; the four fact tiles (Dedicated: a person fills the seat and works only on your company; Offshore: the person works offshore, fully remote; Your roles: you choose the roles you need; Steered by WE: WE steers the team and manages the subcontractors who fill the seats, so you work with one team instead of coordinating individuals); 'The seat is the unit of work' paragraph and the notice sentence. The Offshore tile joins the original 'works offshore' with the FactBand value 'Fully remote' that sat on the same page. Seat roles come from src/scripts/team-composer.ts.
sources.methodology_limitations: The original paragraph was split into four tiles. Wording is the original's, with 'Fully remote' added from the page's own FactBand.

sources.title: What the page does not publish, and how to ask
sources.exact_url_or_locator: src/content/pages/pricing/pricing.mdx at wp/40, section 'What this page does not show' and the FAQ answer 'Is there a price list?'
sources.next_review: When WE publishes a rate (FLAG-PRICE) or sets a reply policy
sources.variables_units_scope: NotPublished: amounts are not listed; a package has no seat count on the page; WE shares the current rate when asked, so the figure is the one that applies today; the way to ask is the contact form with topic seat-rate. The three steps restate that path: open the form, say what the rate is for (a package, a custom seat plan or the add-on), WE shares the figure. The block says 'the add-on' and does not name it, so the Investor Introductions disclaimer rule is not triggered by it.
sources.methodology_limitations: No reply time is promised. The sentence 'This page lists no amounts. WE shares the current rate ... today.' is kept verbatim in pricing.mdx because the counsel checklist (RELEASE.md, CR-12) quotes it.
sources.freshness_trigger: Any change to FLAG-PRICE or to how the rate is requested
